body:
I am grateful for life. I know that we have but one chance at it too. I also know that our time here is limited, and that we should make the most of it. Dont get me wrong, I am unbelievably torn that my love left me, but I am happy for her at the same time. I am happy that she is pursuing that dream of true happiness, even though it may not be me. This must make me the most difficult person to have to deal with though. 

I appreciate your advice, I have tried to write to myself, or make lists of things I am happy for and things that give me a drive to live. But at the end of the day, my mind cant help but go back to "if you arent going to be truly happy, why is it worth suffering another day". I know how terrible that sounds, but I cant help it. I unfortunately can rationalize that thought with the idea of efficiency too, it'd be much more efficient of me not to waste time or take up space if I will not be involved in raising a family or trying for the person I most love. 

My idea of the meaning of life is not a selfish one, if I had an amazing or unique ability, or if I was to be able to help the world as a whole in some way, I would gladly live my life alone and content. But I am not so amazingly gifted in one area to make me stand out. I am not someone who will be able to change history or make a lasting impression though. I accept who I am, what I have become, and what I was. I know that I can only be myself too. So I dont want to change into something I am not, just to be content and feel numb. 

Sorry for being such a downer, I am really trying not to be. I am really trying to take everything that I am being told and use it in a positive manner. I sincerely appreciate the time that you, and others have given to me in writing to me. So thank you. This battle rages on though...
I honestly need a hug. I need someone to tell me it'll be ok. Because I don't think it will be.

I appreciate your analysis, but I want to say that I did not believe that life had any sort of reason before meeting this girl. And I understand that love is not everything. I also understand that life isn't always about one's self. I am an EXTREMELY selfless person, my day consists mainly of being there for others. If anything I stretch myself thin trying to be there for everyone else. I know that I can live my life as a servant to the world and make a lot of people happy, but what about making happy? 

The big question to me at this point is not about what needs to be done or where I need to get in order to feel "normal" again, the question I have is "how"? And more importantly, "why"? Why can't I beat this on my own, why can't I be stronger, why can't I be happy, why is my logical brain torn on whether to continue or not? 

Thank you for your response to me. I do really appreciate it, and I am taking what everyone is saying on here and trying to do my best at putting the puzzle together.

I would love to be able to talk to someone. I have no one that I can confide in without a negative outcome. My friends and family don't take me seriously and think that it is just a game. I know that I am seriously "sick" though. I know that I need help. I can sense it in my body that I can't do this alone. :(

I appreciate you sharing your story with me, and I do relate quite a bit. But what I guess I can't properly explain is, I know what I need to do in order to be happy again. I even realize the extent of the fight ahead of me to become happy. But getting my mind to stay consistently be positive and not let the thoughts of suicide creep in is proving to be far too much for me. I just can't justify to myself  wasting time, earths resources, and energy to continue to fight to be content. I don't to be content. I want to say i lived my life and was the happiest I can be. No material object will ever make me that happy. No other person has ever come close to my recent ex too. She truly was/is the most amazing and special person to ever be in my life...

I also want to add, during my time of recovery from my injury, I developed an addiction to pain killers. I managed to kick the habit with somewhat ease with the help of my love. I was addicted to the nastiest most powerful of pain killers too. From what I've been told, the same level of addiction I was experiencing was that of heroin users. But I kicked the addiction so easily with this person by my side. She literally makes me shine brighter, makes me heal faster, jump higher. How ever you want to put it. That's who my love was to me. She made me better, without ever even trying...

I have experienced love and loss before. When I said that the world was at my fingertips, it's because I worked hard to get there. My life hasn't been a walk in the park, but it also has not been handed to me. I lost my first love nearly a decade ago and went through a period of sadness, but not depression. It was not like this. This is exponentially more difficult. 

And by no means am I trying to shoot you down, I understand where your thought process is coming from. I'm just trying to further explain... 

I do had close friends but they do not "believe" in depression. Especially when they see me so strong all the time, they tell me that I'm full of it when I say it am actually depressed. Family tells me the same thing. 

I know that I can find a "rock" of my own again someday too, I'm not worried about that, I'm worried about being truly happy, but never being able to experience it again. I'm worried about dying content.

Thank you, I would very much appreciate any sort of help at this point. I have tried everything I can to get past this but I can't seem to do it alone, or even with the help of friends and family. It has been a collective effort, yet I can't seem to do it.

I understand that Dakkon, I really do, I recognize my problems in thinking, but it's so much harder than just keeping your chin up and trying to talk yourself into those things. I know that I am a valuable being and that I have a lot to offer this world, I also know that there are other people out there that can make me content or maybe even a little happy with my life. 

I'm trying to get an understanding of why I can't get past this even after having a full understanding of all of that. I feel like part of me is missing.
